item: U-1 | Measured effect of AI trial matching on accrual rate in a controlled comparison (assignment item 5)
queries_tried: WebSearch: 'artificial intelligence clinical trial matching measured effect on accrual rate prospective controlled comparison screening efficiency oncology study'; WebSearch: 'AI in Oncology Clinical Research Accelerating Patient Matching'; WebFetch: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41512229/ ; WebFetch: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13091143/ ; WebSearch: 'expert validation artificial intelligence enabled trial matching real-world data patients with cancer'
failure_reason: No published study located that compares accrual rate under AI matching against a concurrent non-AI control arm. Every accessible evaluation uses matching accuracy (F1, sensitivity, specificity) or screening time as the endpoint. The one deployment reporting actual enrolments (E-5047) is a single-institution observational rollout with no concurrent manual-screening comparator, so its 117 enrolments cannot be attributed to the AI. PubMed returned a cookie-consent wall on direct fetch; the PMC full text of the prospective 3,804-patient study explicitly states enrolment was not an endpoint.
alt_sources_tried: (1) PubMed record 41512229 for the CTPM system - blocked by cookie wall, recovered via search snippet only. (2) PMC13091143 full text (ESMO Real World Data and Digital Oncology, prospective n=3804) - retrieved in full; reports no downstream enrolment counts. (3) ASCO abstract 10.1200/JCO.2026.44.16_suppl.1501 'Expert validation of an AI-enabled trial matching solution' - validation-against-expert design, no accrual endpoint. (4) Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology 's41571-026-01189-0' AI-based augmentation of oncology clinical trials - review, no controlled accrual data. (5) SYNERGY-AI registry NCT03452774 - registry design, no comparator.
best_estimate: No credible controlled accrual effect exists as of 2026-08-18. The honest current figure is 117 enrolments from 98,348 charts screened across 29 trials over ~3.5 years, a 0.12% chart-to-enrolment yield, alongside a 10-fold reduction in chart-review workload and a 41% reduction in per-chart screening time.
best_estimate_basis: E-5047 (CTPM deployment, only source reporting enrolments), E-5048 (prospective n=3804, matching accuracy only), E-5067 (derived ratio). Mechanistic reasoning: AI reduces the marginal cost of identifying candidates; the observed yield stayed at 0.12% because the binding resource is open matching slots at qualified sites, not identified patients. A controlled study would therefore be expected to show a large screening-cost effect and a small accrual effect.

item: U-2 | TAPUR screening denominator and therefore its match rate (assignment item 4)
queries_tried: WebSearch: 'TAPUR study ASCO enrollment match rate number of patients enrolled cohorts results 2024'; inspection of https://www.asco.org/research-data/tapur-study/study-results and https://society.asco.org/research-data/tapur-study/eligibility-enrollment result summaries
failure_reason: ASCO publishes cumulative enrolment (~3,000 since 2016) and site count (260+) but does not publish, on any accessible page, the number of patients whose genomic reports were reviewed for a match. Without that denominator no match rate can be computed. TAPUR also differs structurally from NCI-MATCH: patients arrive with a commercial genomic report already in hand, so the screening funnel is partly external to the study and may not be countable even in principle.
alt_sources_tried: (1) ASCO TAPUR study-results and eligibility-enrollment pages - enrolment only. (2) Targeted Oncology 'TAPUR Results Roll Out' coverage - cohort-level response data, no screening denominator. (3) AJMC coverage of the TAPUR immunotherapy expansion - no denominator. (4) PMC4570058 (ASCO/NCI precision medicine trial launch) - design paper predating accrual.
best_estimate: TAPUR match rate 30-60%, materially higher than NCI-MATCH's 17.8%.
best_estimate_basis: Bracketed by three measured anchors: NCI-MATCH assigned 17.8% of centrally screened patients and 26.4% had all sub-protocols been open simultaneously (E-5028); Lung-MAP registered 37.6% of screened patients to a sub-study (E-5029). TAPUR sits above both because its patients self-select on already having a commercial genomic report and because its drugs are marketed agents with broad label coverage, removing two of the three attrition steps present in NCI-MATCH. The upper bound of 60% reflects that clinical exclusion criteria and cohort-closure still apply.

item: U-3 | Measured realised accrual change attributable to FDA/ASCO eligibility-broadening initiatives (assignment item 2)
queries_tried: WebSearch: 'ASCO FDA broadening eligibility criteria measured effect increase eligible population accrual modernizing eligibility criteria study percentage'; WebSearch: '"Broadening Eligibility Criteria and Diversity among Patients for Cancer Clinical Trials" NEJM Evidence 2024 78% increase eligible'; WebFetch: https://evidence.nejm.org/doi/pdf/10.1056/EVIDoa2300236 (HTTP 403)
failure_reason: All located quantifications are simulated eligibility applied retrospectively to real-world cohorts, not observed accrual after implementation. The NEJM Evidence study computes how many more patients would have qualified; it does not follow trials that adopted broadened criteria and measure their accrual against matched trials that did not. The NEJM PDF returned HTTP 403; the numbers were recovered from the journal abstract page and the Flatiron publication summary.
alt_sources_tried: (1) NEJM Evidence full-text and PDF - 403 Forbidden; abstract-level numbers recovered via search. (2) AACR Clinical Cancer Research ASCO-Friends joint research statement (27:9:2394) - recommendations, no post-implementation measurement. (3) Friends of Cancer Research eligibility-criteria programme pages - advocacy and recommendation content. (4) ASCO Connection interview with Dr Edward S. Kim and the 2019 ASCO 10,500-patient NSCLC analysis - modelled exclusion avoidance, conference abstract. (5) The ASCO Post coverage of the July 2026 FDA final guidances - policy news, no effect measurement.
best_estimate: Realised accrual improvement of 5-15% where the ASCO-Friends recommendations are fully adopted, i.e. a small fraction of the 78% modelled eligibility gain.
best_estimate_basis: Three quantified constraints on conversion. (a) The 78% eligibility gain is simulated (E-5015) and the newly eligible have worse real-world survival, HR 1.31, so sponsors have a direct incentive not to adopt fully. (b) Over half of early-phase oncology screen failures are radiological or biological disease-state changes between consent and treatment (E-5013), which broadened criteria cannot address. (c) In the NCI trial cohort the measured association between criteria complexity and accrual failure is OR 1.09 per decile (E-5012), implying that moving a trial from the top to the bottom complexity decile changes accrual-failure odds by roughly a factor of 2 on a base of 19.3%, i.e. a recovery of order 10 percentage points of trials, not 78%.

item: U-4 | Full year-by-year CDER IND receipt series 2015-2025 in machine-readable form (assignment item 6)
queries_tried: WebSearch: 'FDA CDER commercial IND applications received per year statistics annual report 2015 2020 2024 number of INDs'; WebSearch: '"IND receipts" CDER commercial 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 table number annual growth'; WebSearch: '"INDs with activity" CDER commercial research total number active INDs 2015 2020 2025 growth'; WebFetch: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/ind-activity-reports/ind-receipts (HTTP 401); WebFetch: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/ind-activity/inds-activity (HTTP 401); WebFetch: https://www.fda.gov/media/191373/download (HTTP 401)
failure_reason: fda.gov returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized to the available fetch tooling on every path attempted, including the IND Receipts landing page, the INDs with Activity page, and the /media/{id}/download report endpoints. curl and wget are prohibited by environment rule E2, so no alternative retrieval path exists from this session. Two anchor years (2018 commercial 852 / research 742; 2024 commercial 1,139 / research 716) were recovered from search-result snippets that render the FDA table headers and rows directly, plus one secondary compilation. The INDs-with-activity series was recovered in full for 2020-2025.
alt_sources_tried: (1) FDA IND Receipts landing page - 401. (2) FDA INDs with Activity page - 401. (3) FDA media download endpoints 191373, 191374, 135133, 135166, 185466, 185467 - 401 on direct fetch; row content for 2018 and 2025 legible in search-result titles. (4) bla-regulatory.com secondary compilation - retrieved successfully, supplied INDs with activity 2020-2024 and 2024 receipts, explicitly states it lacks a multi-year receipt series. (5) FDA Annual CDER Reports to Congress index - located but individual PDFs sit behind the same 401.
best_estimate: Intervening years 2019-2023 lie on a roughly log-linear path between 852 (2018) and 1,139 (2024) commercial receipts, i.e. approximately 894, 939, 985, 1,034 and 1,085. Compound growth 4.96%/yr.
best_estimate_basis: E-5050 (two verified anchor years), E-5061 (derived CAGR). Cross-checked for consistency against the independently recovered and complete INDs-with-activity series (E-5049), which grew 3.18%/yr over 2020-2025 - a lower rate than receipts, as expected since the active stock integrates receipts against terminations and withdrawals. The missing intervening years affect only the precision of the CAGR, not its sign or order of magnitude, and no conclusion in the report depends on any single intervening year.
